title: Living and Non-living Things
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Living and Non-living Things Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Compare characteristics of living and non-living things and examine the differences between the life cycles of plants and animals (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on living and non-living things: what all living things do, and sorting things into living, dead (once alive) and never alive. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things grow, feed and reproduce.
key_sub: Moving is not enough: a living thing grows, needs food, water and air, responds and reproduces.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things share features that non-living things do not have.

  • Living things need food (or make it), water and air; they grow, respond to changes, get rid of waste, reproduce and die.
  • Dead things were once alive: a dry leaf, a shell, wood, cotton.
  • Never-alive things were never part of a living thing: rock, plastic, metal, glass, water.
Example

A car moves. Is it alive?

it cannot grow or reproduce

Answer: no

Example

A wooden spoon: living, dead or never alive?

wood comes from a tree

Answer: dead (once alive)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking anything that moves is alive (cars, wind, fire).
  • Thinking plants are not alive because they do not walk.
  • Putting wood, paper or wool in 'never alive'.

faq.q: What makes something a living thing?
faq.a: Living things need food, water and air. They grow, respond to changes, get rid of waste and reproduce.
No. Fire can grow and move, but it does not reproduce, respond or grow like a living thing.
Dead means something was once alive but is not alive now, such as a dry leaf, a shell or a piece of wood.

items.q: Is a wooden boomerang living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It came from something that was alive.

items.q: Which one of these is a living thing?
items.e: An earthworm needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.

items.q: Is a gum tree alive even though it cannot walk?
c: Yes. It grows, takes in water and makes seeds.
items.e: Plants are living things.

items.q: Is a campfire flame living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Is a steel fence living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A cloud does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A remote-control car does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: A seed is in a packet. Is it alive?
c: Yes, it is alive but resting until it gets water and warmth.
items.e: Seeds can grow into new plants.

items.q: Is a koala living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It grows, needs food, water and air, and reproduces.

items.q: Which one of these is a living thing?
items.e: A kitten needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A bicycle does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: A toy robot is a non-living thing, although it makes sounds. Which of these can it NOT do?
items.e: Only living things can reproduce (make young or new plants).

items.q: Why is a wooden table 'dead' and not 'never alive'?
c: The wood came from a tree that was once alive.
items.e: Wood, paper and cotton came from living things.

items.q: Which of these can reproduce?
items.e: Living things make more of their own kind.

items.q: A car moves and uses fuel. Why is it not alive?
c: It moves, so it is alive.
It is made of metal, so it is alive.
items.e: Moving is not enough to be alive.

items.e: Only living things can reproduce (make young or new plants).

items.q: Is a seashell on the beach living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It came from something that was alive.

items.q: A ceiling fan is a non-living thing, although it moves. Which of these can it NOT do?
items.e: Only living things can reproduce (make young or new plants).

items.q: A car is a non-living thing, although it moves and uses fuel. Which of these can it NOT do?
items.e: Only living things can reproduce (make young or new plants).

items.q: Is a gum tree living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It grows, needs food, water and air, and reproduces.

items.q: Kai says a toy robot is alive because it moves. What is wrong?
c: A robot cannot feed, grow or have young, so it is not alive.
Robots are alive because they move.
items.e: Living things can move by themselves. Plants move slowly, for example turning to the light.

items.q: A balsam plant makes seeds that grow into new plants. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows reproduction.

items.q: A rock cannot have young. What does this tell us?
items.e: Living things make new living things like them.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things need?
items.e: Plants make food; animals eat food.

items.q: Which of these shows that a chicken reproduces?
c: It lays eggs that hatch into chicks.
items.e: Reproducing means making young.

items.q: A fern makes spores that grow into new ferns. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows reproduction.

items.q: A cockroach runs away when the light is switched on. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows response to changes.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things take in air.

items.q: A rock cannot grow. What does this tell us?
items.e: Living things get bigger as they get older.

items.q: A balsam plant wilts when it is not watered. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows the need for water.

items.q: A hen lays eggs that hatch into chicks. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows reproduction.

items.q: Which of these shows that a cat responds to changes?
c: It runs away when a dog barks.
items.e: Responding means reacting to something around it.

items.q: A dog drinks from its bowl after a run. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows the need for water.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things can move by themselves. Plants move slowly, for example turning to the light.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things make new living things like them.

items.q: A mosquito sucks blood to get food. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows the need for food.

items.q: Which shows that a plant responds to changes?
c: Its leaves turn towards the light.
items.e: Living things respond.

items.q: A plant on a windowsill bends towards the light. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows response to changes.

items.q: Which living thing does NOT move from place to place?
items.e: Plants are living but do not move from place to place.

items.q: Which of these shows that a mango tree grows?
c: It becomes taller and thicker over the years.
items.e: Growing means getting bigger over time.

items.q: Is a dry gum leaf on the ground living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It came from something that was alive.

items.q: A seed looks like a tiny stone. Is it alive?
c: Yes. It can grow into a new plant.
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: Is a frog living, dead or never alive?
items.e: It is living: it can feed, grow and breathe.

items.q: Is a plastic bucket living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Is a glass bottle living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Is a rock at Uluru living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Is a woolly jumper living, dead or never alive?
items.e: It came from something that was once alive.

items.q: A tree does not walk. Is it alive?
c: Yes. It feeds, grows and makes seeds.
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: Is a twig on the ground living, dead or never alive?
items.e: It came from something that was once alive.

items.q: Is a wooden table living, dead or never alive?
items.e: It came from something that was once alive.

items.q: Is a sunflower living, dead or never alive?
items.e: It is living: it can feed, grow and breathe.

items.q: Which group is a rock in?
items.e: Rocks are not part of living things.

items.q: Fire grows and moves. Is it alive?
c: No. It does not feed, breathe and have young like living things.
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: A cloud moves across the sky. Is it alive?
c: No. It is made of water, which was never alive.
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: Is a steel can living, dead or never alive?
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Paper is made from trees. Which group is paper in?
items.e: Trees were once alive.

items.q: What does 'living' mean?
c: it is made in a factory
alive now: it feeds, grows, breathes and has young
items.e: Animals and plants are living.

items.q: Which of these was never alive: a horse, a leather shoe, a plastic bottle or a worm?
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Mia kept a potted plant in a dark cupboard and gave it no water for 3 weeks. What most likely happened?
c: The plant grew taller and greener.
items.e: Living things need water to survive.

items.q: Which of these gets rid of waste?
items.e: Living things get rid of waste.

items.q: Are plants alive?
c: Yes. They feed, grow and make seeds.
items.e: Plants are living things.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of all living things?
items.e: Most living things cannot talk.

items.q: Which of these is living: a growing tomato plant, a pebble, a plastic ball or a steel can?
items.e: It is living: it can feed, grow and breathe.

items.q: What does 'dead' mean?
c: it was once alive but is not alive now
items.e: A dead leaf was once alive.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A toy robot does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Which of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A stone does not need food or reproduce.

items.q: Why is a wooden table non-living now?
c: It was once part of a tree but no longer grows or reproduces.
It was never part of a living thing.
items.e: The wood came from a living tree, but the table is not alive.

items.q: Why is a fire NOT a living thing, even though it grows bigger?
c: It does not reproduce or respond like a living thing.
items.e: A thing must show all the characteristics of living things.

items.q: Do plants need air?
c: Yes. All living things, including plants, need air.
Only plants that have flowers need air.
items.e: Plants need air, just like animals.

items.q: Which of these shows that a plant needs water?
c: A plant that is not watered wilts.
A plant grows in a pot.
items.e: Without water, a plant wilts and may die.

items.q: Which of these is living: a cardboard box, a lump of clay, a paper book or a magpie?
items.e: It is living: it can feed, grow and breathe.

items.q: Which of these was never alive: a daisy, a leather shoe, a seashell on the beach or a toy car?
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Which of these living things lays eggs?
items.e: Chickens reproduce by laying eggs; dogs, cows and cats give birth to young.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A plastic bottle does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Which of these is dead (was once alive): a bone, a frog, a ladybird or a pebble?
items.e: It came from something that was once alive.

items.q: A sunflower turns towards the light. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: The plant reacts to the light.

items.q: A puppy becomes an adult dog. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows growth.

items.q: Is a dog living, dead or never alive?
items.e: It is living: it can feed, grow and breathe.

items.q: A student put a cardboard box with a hole over a potted plant. After a week, the plant had bent towards the hole. Why?
c: The plant responds to light by growing towards it.
The plant moved to find water.
items.e: Plants respond to light.

items.q: Is sea water living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It was never part of a living thing.

items.q: Ruby sorts items into 'living', 'dead' and 'never alive'. Where should she put a feather?
items.e: Feathers come from birds.

items.q: Priya put some mealworms in a box with one dark end and one bright end. Most mealworms moved to the dark end. What does this show?
items.e: The mealworms reacted to the light by moving away.

items.q: A student sealed a small plant in an airtight jar and another in an open jar. Which plant is likely to stay healthy longer?
c: the plant in the sealed jar
the plant in the open jar
items.e: Plants need air to stay alive.

items.q: Is a fallen log living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It came from something that was alive.

items.q: Which observation would show that a snail is living?
c: It is found in the garden.
items.e: Growth is a characteristic of living things.

items.q: Kai watches a snail for 10 minutes. It moves away when he touches it. Which feature of living things does this show?

items.q: Two identical guppies were kept in tanks. One was fed; one was not fed for a long time. What does this experiment test?
c: whether guppies need food to stay alive
items.e: Only the food was different.

items.q: A student watered one balsam plant every day and gave another no water. Everything else was the same. What is she finding out?
c: whether plants need water to survive
items.e: Only the water was different.

items.q: A woolly jumper is made from sheep's wool. Which group is it in?
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: Jack sees something moving in a pond. How could he decide if it is alive?
c: Watch whether it feeds, grows, breathes and responds.
items.e: Use the features of living things.

items.q: Is a mushroom living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It grows, needs food, water and air, and reproduces.

items.q: A wooden chair was made from a tree. Which group is it in?
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: A gum tree seedling becomes a big tree. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows growth.

items.q: A car moves. Is it alive?
c: No. It cannot feed, grow or have young.
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: Is a magpie living, dead (once alive) or never alive?
c: a living thing that is asleep
items.e: It grows, needs food, water and air, and reproduces.

items.q: Mia puts bean seeds on wet cotton wool and on dry cotton wool. Only the wet seeds sprout. What does this show?
c: Seeds need water to start growing.
items.e: Living things need water.
